script: I was invited, but my cousin's mom uninvited me—now I am torn.. I booked my flight two weeks before the wedding and already paid for the hotel, so the trip was set. My cousin, a 35-year-old guy, was tying the knot with a fiancée from abroad, and I thought, "Okay, I'll be there." Fast forward to the weekend of the argument. Mom and his mom—my aunt—started yelling over something that had nothing to do with the ceremony. They're both strong‑wired, so it blew up fast. I wasn't there, but I heard enough to know my aunt told Mom to stay away from the wedding. Mom felt like she'd been uninvited. (You're probably thinking, "Is that even a thing?") Yes. My aunt has always been the family drama queen, so the vibe was already off. My cousin didn't say a word about it, and I don't know if he even knows what went down. The wedding is still his, not his mom's, but my mom's exclusion makes the whole thing feel weird. I never really wanted to go. If I'd known this before buying tickets, I'd have said no. But I already committed. Canceling now feels like throwing a wrench in the plans. So I am stuck: - Mom isn't welcome, so why should I be there? - If Mom just decided to skip it, I'd be fine. - But she was told no. I can still show up, support the happy couple, and stay away from my aunt. I can keep it chill and not stir drama. Would I go? I'd probably stay. The wedding isn't my issue; it's the disrespect my mom felt. If Mom's not there, the whole "family" thing loses its meaning. I'd let the couple celebrate and keep my own boundaries intact. So, yeah, I am thinking of ditching the trip. The wedding is his day, but my mom deserves respect, not a forced absence.
